title: A Detention for the Yearbook
premise: Rosalind Almeida has survived ten years at Hollow Creek High by being forgettable, pouring everything she can't say into the bread she bakes for the school café. When journalism teacher Ms. Okafor pairs her with Theo Vance—the boy whose family's construction company built the school's crumbling east wing—for a semester-long investigative project, their mutual hatred curdles into something more dangerous: proof. Together they discover the school board knew the wing was structurally failing years ago and buried the report, and Rosalind's own late mother's signature is on the original inspection. As the board moves to demolish the evidence along with the wing, Rosalind must choose between staying safe and publishing the truth in the yearbook's final pages, even if it means her mother's memory becomes a casualty. In the end, the story runs, the east wing is condemned and rebuilt, and Rosalind—no longer invisible—finds a found family in Theo, Ms. Okafor, and the misfit yearbook staff who refused to stay quiet.
about_author: Xanthe Fairweather is a former high school newspaper adviser who spent seven years watching teenagers uncover truths adults preferred buried. She writes in a converted bakery in coastal Maine, where the smell of sourdough still finds its way into every manuscript.

chapters.title: The Careful Life of Rosalind Almeida
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. We meet her rules for invisibility as she bakes grief-bread for her father's café and navigates Hollow Creek High without a single ripple. Emotional beat: the ache of being safe and lonely at once.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ms. Okafor pairs her with Theo Vance for the semester investigative project; their first meeting is open warfare, each blaming the other's family for the east wing's decay. Emotional beat: fury masking fear of being truly seen.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Plaster
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, desperate to prove his family name isn't cursed, drags Rosalind into the east wing and shows her the hairline fractures he's been photographing for a year. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance over shared dread.

chapters.title: What Mother Signed
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Digging through her late mother's inspection reports for the project, Rosalind finds her mother's signature on the 2014 structural assessment—and a page torn out. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of her grief.

chapters.title: Detention, Room 114
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Caught trespassing in the east wing after hours, both are sentenced to weekly detention with Ms. Okafor, who suspiciously asks no questions and leaves the archive unlocked. Emotional beat: the first hint that an adult is on their side.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Misfits
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Detention introduces them to the yearbook staff: Priya the archivist, Dez the photographer, and Sam the dropout-risk editor who knows every locked door in the building. Emotional beat: the terrifying warmth of belonging to something.

chapters.title: Bread for Enemies
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rosalind brings apology-rye to a late-night work session; Theo, whose father starves him of approval, doesn't know how to accept kindness and ruins the moment. Emotional beat: two damaged kids speaking different languages of care.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Priya recovers the missing 2014 page from microfiche: the wing was rated for immediate closure, and the board's then-chairman—now state senator—ordered it suppressed. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear of how big this is.

chapters.title: Vance & Sons
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his father about the shoddy 2019 patch-job his company did to hide the cracks, and learns his father was threatened into silence. Emotional beat: the corruption of power reaching inside Theo's own home.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Our Drafts
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Their shared drive is wiped, Ms. Okafor is suddenly reassigned to 'administrative leave,' and a board lawyer visits the school. Emotional beat: paranoia—the price of survival means someone is watching.

chapters.title: The Bake Sale Gambit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. To rebuild their evidence, the team hides documents in plain sight: Rosalind bakes them into hollowed loaves sold at the café, coded by flavor. Emotional beat: defiant joy—turning her invisibility craft into armor.

chapters.title: Sam's Secret
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam reveals they were in the east wing the day a ceiling tile fell and injured a student three years ago—a cover-up Sam was paid to keep quiet about. Emotional beat: guilt and the corrupting price of survival money.

chapters.title: Demolition Order
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The board fast-tracks east wing demolition for the last week of school—before the yearbook prints. The evidence, and the truth, will be buried in rubble. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a monster.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Is Afraid Of
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A quiet chapter: at her mother's grave, Rosalind admits she's terrified the report proves her mother was complicit, not heroic. Theo listens without fixing it. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared brokenness.

chapters.title: The Bribe
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A board representative offers Theo a full-ride scholarship and Rosalind's father a café lease renewal—in exchange for a 'satisfactory' project and silence. Emotional beat: temptation, and the taste of power trying to buy them.

chapters.title: Refusals
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind declines; her father, learning everything, tells her her mother would have published. Theo's refusal costs him his father's door. Emotional beat: the family you're born into versus the one you choose.

chapters.title: Print Deadline
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. The yearbook staff works a feverish all-nighter, laying out the investigation across sixteen pages, knowing the printer may be leaned on to kill the run. Emotional beat: exhausted, sacred solidarity.

chapters.title: The Printer Problem
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The print shop cancels their order under pressure; the team scrambles, and Dez's older sister offers her community-college press—at a cost they can barely cover. Emotional beat: desperation met by community.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The night before distribution, Rosalind is locked in the east wing archive by someone searching for the master documents; she escapes through the crumbling corridor as a section of ceiling gives way. Emotional beat: raw terror—survival has a literal price now.

chapters.title: Distribution Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Yearbooks hit the halls; the board tries to confiscate them, but students pass them hand to hand, and local press arrives before first period ends. Emotional beat: the roar of a quiet girl finally heard.

chapters.title: Hearings and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The senator resigns, an independent inspection confirms everything, and Theo's father testifies—rebuilding their relationship brick by brick. Rosalind's mother is posthumously cleared; she'd tried to report the suppression. Emotional beat: grief reframed as pride.

chapters.title: A Loaf for the New Wing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the groundbreaking for the rebuilt wing, Rosalind bakes bread for her found family—Theo, Sam, Priya, Dez, and Ms. Okafor, back from leave. She writes the yearbook's final line herself. Emotional beat: visible, chosen, home.
